checks.label: Every new formula undoes its old one and gives back the letter's example value: I = V ÷ R, R = V ÷ I, V = I × R, I = P ÷ V, x = (y − 5) ÷ 3, t = (v − u) ÷ a, u = v − at, a = (v − u) ÷ t, V = P ÷ I; every card's values fit it, 12 = 3 × 4, 16 = 2 × 8, 2300 = 230 × 10, 26 = 3 × 7 + 5, 18 = 6 + 3 × 4; and v = 20, u = 8, a = 4 give t = 3, with 8 + 4 × 3 = 20

They all are combinations of just two equations, Ohm's law and power: V = IR put into P = VI gives P = I²R for the amounts on every electrical card, with R = V ÷ I where a card has no R (23 Ω for 2300 W at 230 V)

The change side, change sign method works absolutely perfectly for a great number of equations: wherever the step that crosses over is a + or a −, it gives the same new formula as undoing on both sides

To change the subject of a formula the terms are rearranged following the general rule, change side, change operation: each step crossing over as its opposite operation, last step first, gives every new formula on these screens, and every check matches
Reach the equation x / 4 = 160 correctly, then x = 160/4: dividing where it should multiply gives 40, and 40 / 4 is 10, not 160; multiplying gives 640, and 640 / 4 = 160

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives, its check failing: change side, change sign used on a × or a ÷; a step done again instead of undone; a divide the wrong way round; only part of a side divided; or the × undone before the +

Every picture, finished, draws the steps in order from the letter wanted, each undo box under the step it undoes with the opposite steps lit, then the new formula and its check; the change side screen fails its check and units in the warning colour; and a wrong answer's formula and check fail in the warning colour, clear of the check's name
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer: no undo box lit, no new formula, no value for the letter

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart
